pick.name: Apache-2.0 core + proprietary ee/ folder, DCO sign-off
pick.what: Permissive core for adoption (SDKs, MCP servers, plugins), paid features in a separately licensed folder, DCO on PRs
pick.why: Maximises adoption and Claude-ecosystem trust; DCO is lighter than a CLA and enough when you never need to relicense contributed core code
pick.free_limits: DCO GitHub app (third-party, pricing not stated)

alts.name: FSL-1.1-ALv2 (Functional Source License)
alts.what: Fair-source: anything except competing use; each version becomes Apache-2.0 after 2 years
alts.why: Best for a hosted SaaS where a clone is the main risk; not OSI open source

alts.name: AGPL-3.0 + CLA Assistant (dual licensing)
alts.what: Copyleft core, sell commercial licences; CLA lets you relicense contributions
alts.why: Strongest anti-cloud-clone protection that is still OSI open source; free hosted CLA bot by SAP

candidates.name: Apache-2.0 + ee/
candidates.verdict: PICK for SDKs, MCP servers, plugins, CLIs

candidates.name: FSL-1.1-ALv2
candidates.verdict: Pick for a hosted SaaS app's own source

candidates.name: AGPL-3.0 + CLA
candidates.verdict: Pick if you want OSI-approved but clone-resistant + dual licensing

candidates.name: BSL 1.1
candidates.verdict: Similar to FSL but longer change dates; FSL is simpler

candidates.name: Elastic-2.0
candidates.verdict: Source-available; blocks managed-service resale (Mintlify CLI uses it)

candidates.name: MIT
candidates.verdict: Fine for small libraries; no patent grant

decision: Use Apache-2.0 + DCO for anything meant to spread (SDKs, MCP servers, Claude plugins), and FSL for the SaaS app itself if you open its source. Choose AGPL + CLA only if you plan to sell commercial licences.
details: Licence choice has legal consequences; verify with a lawyer.

verify.note: Reasonable standard advice. Only shallow checks: DCO app page and FSL not fetched. Dub (alt elsewhere) is confirmed AGPL outside its (ee) folders.
